title: Moon-forming giant impact
note: Child of formation of Earth; perspectives on canonical, synestia, multiple-impact and immediate-satellite models; timing 40-150 Myr after CAIs (Raymond 2024; NASA; Kegerreis et al. 2022).

title: Oldest known terrestrial zircon, Jack Hills, Western Australia
note: Wilde et al. 2001 Nature (4,404 ± 8 Myr); IUGS geoheritage site Erawondoo Hill; on Wajarri Yamaji country, check Indigenous place names and later re-dating (Valley et al. 2014).

title: Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains greenstone belt and early life traces
note: UNESCO World Heritage site (South Africa/Eswatini); some of the best-preserved 3.6-3.25 Ga crust, meteorite-impact spherule beds and early microbial traces. Fills an empty Africa x Archean cell.

title: Acasta Gneiss, oldest known rocks
note: About 4.03 Ga (USGS); ICS base of Archean 4031 ± 3 Ma. On Tlicho lands, Northwest Territories; record the Indigenous names of the Acasta River area.

title: Clair Patterson
note: Age of Earth 1953/1956 at Caltech and later campaign against environmental lead from petrol; pin the 1956 paper and the leaded-fuel work as separate events.

title: Dresser Formation stromatolites, Pilbara, Western Australia
note: Thread from the Jack Hills crust and oceans to the earliest widely accepted evidence of life; links to -3700my-origin-of-life and the contested Isua (Greenland) claims.
